notes.title: KART Devlog 4
notes.content:
[p]Heeey!!! Been a good while, sorry about the silence! Even though I've got a couple folks helping, it's still primarily just me cracking away at this. Got a new work from home job, so my exhaustion shouldn't deter me from working so much anymore. Let's get into what's new!!!

Well, since we last spoke, I've improved midair physics a bit, so there is a lot more stability![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/3f1cadc26fb546533681dc817f1ac4ca7a4b44a3.gif"][/img][/p][p]There's also some nice lean to your turns now! (was implemented literally 3 days ago)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/0dcdac58997ea81d729846ed05f165cbfdb1c1a5.gif"][/img] 

Just for a moment I'd also like to show off some of the SDK capabilities, using a Vampire Survivors skeleton as an example! (We have no association with those devs, but I'm a big fan. (poncle if you ever hear about KART please let me make a Vampire Survivors track(s)...)) Also, sorry in advance about some of the gif compression on these. Someone once mistook it for an artistic choice.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/f7468dbd4aea9c049b565e2d1bba0549cccc0751.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/b9dfb86f015da2cde3985700873d0a5fc480e84b.gif"][/img][/p][p]
First of all, say hi to Sid! He's a 2D character, based on old original Gameboy graphics. Art direction for this game is going to be a bit weird, so bare with it; we're intentionally going to mix a lot of art styles together. He's of course riding a bike. We can talk more about that later.

So what are you looking at exactly? Well, these skeletons are made by using 100% modding tools! They are made using things you'll have access to. Here's a breakdown of what the skeletons made of:

- Roamer (script to make them move around a point)
- Spawner (script to make multiple of them spawn)
- Detection zone (script to detect the kart and do things...)
- Speed filter (to detect player speed)
- Damage zone (only hits players beneath a certain speed)
- Flinger (flings an object depending on how fast the racer is going)
- Coin effect (to give coins to a racer)
- Timer (waits to respawn the skeleton)
- Tagger (tags players when they kill a skeleton)

That last one feeds into a larger tagging system. You can selectively effect racers by applying tags to them. So, in theory, you could have alternate routes in a track designated for players who have achieved something in particular. You can make the tag visible (see the skeleton tag near the coin counter?), or hide it for more subtle effects.

The tools I'm making will be able to be mixed in matched to create very cool stuff!

Anyways, too many words not enough pictures. Here's some UI in progress here. (The background is a placeholder, unfortunately.) I wanted to make sure the UI was as speedy to navigate as the game is. 

Also busted character in progress there, don't worry about that.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/b40ae288abe6903c5ce39fcf68e574e5a620e6f7.gif"][/img]

Here's something fun too: when playing local split screen, your icon at the bottom of the screen is interactive. This way, you can show all your friends how impatient you are by mashing buttons.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/c919712da5ac83018fa939d19bcb402b3efe3db8.gif"][/img]

"Me and my friends only have enough money for one copy of KART..." no problem bro, maybe get a job, but otherwise just invite up to 7 friends over to play.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/5c0bccb9448198153d135d446be2ea69e8048047.gif"][/img]

You wouldn't believe how hard it is to get audio working for 8 players. A lot of time was poured into that over the last couple months. I tried a lot of stuff, and eventually wound up with something pretty good here. That said, it's still a lot on the processing end, not sure if all systems will be able to handle it, but you're welcome to try.

You may notice the top left player is someone we haven't seen before. His name is Ichigogo, little fella is based on Sanrio characters & art. I think taunting has been in for a while, but it's a good opportunity to show you here.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/42c1fd7659e828c606cccdd44f26d6fe1d7f272c.gif"][/img]

You can perform a taunt by pressing jump while you're at the peak of your midair time. If you keep mashing it, you can drop coins as a flex on your haters.

Ichigogo is a strawberry jam salesdog in his regular life. You can learn about him through the collectable figurine unlockables around the tracks, OR just be a quitter and buy them with the coins you've collected.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/20b853e2ef0c7f02e6a6dd90027a44f1a9e7a090.gif"][/img][/p][p]
Other unlockables will include racers, vehicles, tracks, and sound effects you can use as horns. Probably also skins, but not in the "buy the season pass!!1!1" sort of way. Just fun alt costumes. The whole game is sort of getting a chaotic air about it, and that's kinda the way I want it. So, to encourage the chaos, I'm allowing players to animate the text in the in-game chat.

Online stuff is in the works. I initially planned Steam Workshop for hosting mods but if we ever want to move to a console, we'll want a mod system that is cross-platform, so we're thinking hard about that. There's other little touches and flourishes I've got going on back this way, but I'll keep it in my pocket for now.

I love you guys! Thanks to anybody who has wishlisted KART so far, it's been a long journey but hopefully before long we can laser focus in on some environments and really show you what we've got.

Take care! I'll try not to take so long on the next devlog this time!!![/p]

notes.title: KART Devlog 3
notes.content:
Hey guys! Hopefully you're enjoying this spooky season!

Just wanted to keep progress updates coming here, so I'll show off some of what I've been working on. First thing, I made water look a little prettier, that includes the hydroplaning and underwater visuals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/42f54c2e6689c22c69b0ff8a4798af26b8b6d436.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/2bc1f8d43a159bfe087af4e3107477c5645f6e2f.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/82b1d784dfdc16d8b728ea64a099901c2a564a56.gif[/img]

Still gotta work on some splashy effects when dipping in and out of water, but I think this is a good start.

Also, worked a lot on AI! They can almost do everything you can, and also they can be dumber or smarter than each other. They can drift, use items, look for interesting things on the track, and so on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/9743b5acd557891679851be5685c4ec2387e53cf.gif[/img]

Another thing I've been working on is a track creating tool! I know I said I won't have an in-game editor, but this thing is pretty wacky. You'll be able to access it from the modding SDK I'll be releasing with the demo. Basically it will allow you to drive freely in all three dimensions, and place track behind you. You can tilt, pitch, and change the width of the road. There's also lots of navigation tools like toggling the platform, warping to the start of a segment, and exporting to a file that you can modify in other modeling tools, like Blender. Or, if you aren't satisfied with the mesh it outputs, you can also just export the path data and edit that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/fee38d2288c7361b688bd07780e683ba9913251f.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/5a52c91d07f80b231dc9f19a9e9850e4c0bb758b.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/cd8130431e478ab122561737319a4e70aa756771.gif[/img]

There's also two drive modes in the track editor. You start in Anchored Mode, which is a lot like ModNation Racers' track creation controls. You can toggle Free Mode which allows you to lay track in any way you like. There's also two acceleration modes! First is True Acceleration Mode, which means you're basically just moving around as you would in-game. Alternatively, is Time Acceleration Mode, which you're always travelling at max speed, but the acceleration button controls time rather than your kart's speed. This means you're always laying track as if you were at max speed. This is also based on ModNation Racers' track creation tool.

Anyways, for now that's it! Hopefully everyone has a happy Halloween! I'm going to keep working hard and try to get this thing into your hands soon as I can guarantee it's playable and fun. See ya next time!

notes.title: KART Devlog 2
notes.content:
Hey guys! Just wanted to show off some of the stuff I've been working on these last couple weeks! Firstly, I want to show off a new item; the blade! It's a work in progress still but it's looking and feeling pretty good!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/ae27b864d5276e4e3995379b1aa368ac20b5eac8.gif[/img]

The weapon & trail match your chosen colors, so it ends up looking pretty flashy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/138fd0cd5b5d0f2d6b3fcda964aac10c623fa430.gif[/img]

You can destroy obstacles with it, I still need to amp up the FX for when that happens, but it does the job! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/75f7592874f765360b79f317ec6cdd9484eb0822.gif[/img]

Yep, that's me failing to slice a rocket with it. I wonder what happens when you do it successfully?... Something to think about! You may also notice there's no actual sword model or item icon, but I'll need some more time on that.

I also made a sort of taunt system. If you press the hop button at the height of your jump, you'll do a little taunt. Every time you press the button after that until you land, you'll drop a coin, making it possible to intentionally drop coins. This can be a strategic maneuver, or to give yourself a little handicap, since coins give you a small speed boost.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/be763da43fed2235043bee725aaa70208b6ed480.gif[/img]

Additionally, the UI now supports labels! You can toggle it on and off, of course. Sorry about the quality of the gif on this one, Steam only supports gifs up to 5MB large:

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/494b56227eee88e5f70162100fee7cf11065b922.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/494b56227eee88e5f70162100fee7cf11065b922.gif[/img][/url]

Lastly, conveyor belts! The tools are pretty universal; you can apply this to terrain, or even an entire area to produce a wind effect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/69ad8637f351c634a80870d13d9762758bde37a1.gif[/img]

Ignore the rotation of the tires for now; the animation is just confused because it sees all forward momentum as "driving". I'll fix that and it'll be great! 

The last thing; I added horns & honking to the game. That's not really something you can show off in a gif, but you can effectively use any sound you want since it's integrated into my mod support. I expect folks will be making stuff like "stock sound effect sound pack" mods, and things like that.

That's the development over the last couple weeks! I've got a couple good buddies helping me with the artistic side of the project, meaning some track-related modeling stuff and music, more to come there. Hopefully more stuff to report soon, thanks for checking in on KART and I'm looking forward to delivering everyone a fun game! Take care!

P.S. Today is my birthday! The best present you could get me is spreading the word about my game and making sure it gets lots of wishlists! Thanks everyone, love you lots!

notes.title: KART Devlog 1
notes.content:
Hey everyone! Not sure who may be reading this so early on, but assuming you're seeing it not long after it's published, thanks so much for your interest in the game! Programming-wise, it's just me (Eiko) working on this, and for the majority of the development time, the modelling has all been me as well, so any support is extremely encouraging! Somewhat recently, I hired a 3D artist to help work on tracks, so there's more to come on that front, which I'm very excited about. Working on this game has mostly been a daily grind for me, but of course I've still got to pay my bills with my really cruddy job that pays me peanuts.

Mostly, I'm writing this to sort of communicate where I am with development, so you guys know what to expect. I'm not going to be too comprehensive since it's a lot to cover, but I'm going to quickly go over the key things that are finished and things that still need work.

Most importantly, gameplay feels really nice. I often spend a silly amount of time just drifting around and playing the game because it's satisfying to execute drifts, collect coins, and run into hazards. Currently, races are working very well, and a very simple CPU racer system is also working. So, it's currently possible to race CPU's from start to finish. The CPUs are extremely dumb right now, but they add enough chaos to KART that I have a good idea of how the races against other players will feel. 

That leads me to speak of multiplayer; it's already working! That was one of the first tests I did a while back. Currently it's extremely user-unfriendly to join/host a game, but I've been designing all features with the knowledge that it must work with networking, so I expect minimal adjustments to code I've already written as far as online play is concerned. Eventually I'll get to a point where I can start focusing on lobbies, then I'll actually start looking at having online play tests. I'll probably need some volunteers when that time comes. Wink wink!

While there's still work to be done there, I feel really confident about the actual racing aspect of the game, so for the last few months I've been pouring a lot of my focus into the modding aspect of the game.

As an aside, I already have the spawning system done, so racers and their vehicles can be interchangeable, and you can choose primary and secondary colors for your racer as well.

In regards to modding, I have a system which I'm also feeling really good about. Since I want creators to have as much flexibility as possible, I've decided to not include an editor in-game. My reasoning is that it would limit people to the tools I provide them. Instead, I will be releasing an SDK that can be used to create content for the game via Unity. This means you can make racers, tracks, karts, horn sounds, and maybe more using external tools. So in theory, you should be able to play as whoever you want if you're willing to put forth the effort. In concept, this will effectively be the same as Tabletop Simulator's AssetBundles, if you're familiar with that. 

[b]That said, I will be providing a free demo which people will be able to use to play test their creations without ever owning the full game.[/b] This will happen before the game fully releases, so keep an eye out for that if you're interested! (I might eventually decide to include some sort of editor in-game, but as of right now, that's beyond the scope of this project.)

Also, I'm making the modding tools as simple to use as possible, and I'll be creating tutorials on top of that down the road. 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/0876ea7215e6fc98062998dd4253d1b630f02a44.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44971964/0876ea7215e6fc98062998dd4253d1b630f02a44.gif[/img][/url]

The final result will be a little different than the above, since I've already made a lot of progress since that gif was recorded, but it should be approximately as simple as that. For instance, in the case of custom tracks, you can (selectively or not) apply various effects to racers, as well as implement various interactive elements such as timers, counters, detectors, and so on. There's even a feature where you can trigger events based on the beat of the music.

So anyways, this last week, I've been thinking through the game's startup sequence. That is, from the moment you launch the game until you enter the main menu. The method by which you launch the game is important (from Steam or from Unity via playtest) so that's what I'm working on now. This includes loading the proper things, like achievements or user settings, when the game starts up. I wrote 44 achievements tonight. They're not actually achievable yet, but Steam can acknowledge their existence right now, so that's nice.

Alright, it's 6AM and I gotta get some sleep! Thanks again for your support, I'll keep working hard to bring you all a fun game!
